nodes.content: Build a dependency-upgrade analyzer that distinguishes client-reachable behavioral incompatibilities from harmless upstream changes despite dynamic dispatch and incomplete code.
requirements: Achieve at least 90% recall and 90% precision on 100 labeled upgrade scenarios.
Provide reproducible client-level witnesses for incompatibilities; explicitly identify uncertainty caused by unavailable code or reflection.

nodes.content: Combine dispatch-aware client call graphs with version-differential tests, emitting replayable witnesses and uncertainty tags for reflection or missing code.
How can receiver-type constraints prune virtual-call targets while preserving uncertainty from reflection and missing bytecode?
Allocation-site typing and unknown-target edges for reflection or missing bytecode preserve ≥90% recall while pruning ≥40% dispatch targets.
Build allocation-site call graphs with unknown-target edges; compare dispatch pruning against CHA and recall on 100 labeled upgrades.
Run allocation-site and CHA call graphs on 100 labeled upgrades, measuring dispatch pruning and incompatibility recall with unknown-target edges.
Across 100 labeled upgrades, allocation-site analysis retained 93% incompatibility recall and pruned 47% of CHA dispatch targets.
Adopt allocation-site dispatch with unknown-target edges: 93% recall exceeds the threshold while pruning 47% of CHA targets.
Generate replayable client tests from adopted call graphs, compare dependency versions, and flag missing-code or reflection paths as uncertain.
UpgradeWitness bundle contains replayable client tests, old/new dependency lockfiles, behavioral diffs, and explicit reflection/missing-code uncertainty labels.
Configuration-aware receiver typing with unknown edges for opaque calls will prune ≥50% of CHA targets while retaining ≥90% recall.
Parse service-provider manifests and dependency-injection bindings, then measure configuration-aware dispatch pruning and recall against CHA on 100 labeled upgrades.
Configuration-aware typing pruned 56% of CHA targets but recall fell to 87%; runtime injection overrides escaped parsed bindings.
Reject configuration-only pruning; retain allocation-site analysis with unknown edges because its 93% recall exceeds configuration-aware typing's 87%.
How can replayable client tests separate dependency-caused incompatibilities from nondeterminism and unreachable upstream changes?
Add hermetic differential replay with client-input synthesis, output normalization, and conservative triage of nondeterministic or opaque executions.
Synthesize client-entrypoint inputs, replay each version five times in pinned containers, normalize outputs, and classify only stable reachable divergences.
Execute UpgradeWitness tests under both lockfiles in pinned containers five times each, recording normalized client outputs and flaky-run flags.
ReplayMatrix records five normalized client-output traces per dependency version, container digests, divergence signatures, and flaky-run flags.
Cross-check UpgradeWitness tests against ReplayMatrix traces for 100 labeled upgrades, measuring precision, recall, witness reproducibility, and uncertainty coverage.
Five UpgradeWitness incompatibility witnesses failed pinned replay; on 100 upgrades, hermetic gating raised precision from 84% to 92%.
Does hermetic replay gating miss genuine environment-sensitive incompatibilities and reduce recall below 90%?
Pinned JDK, locale, and timezone variants will recover environment-sensitive witnesses, sustaining ≥90% recall and ≥90% precision.
Rerun 100 labeled upgrades, including five failed witnesses, across pinned JDK, locale, and timezone variants; measure recall and precision.
Across 100 labeled upgrades, environment variants recovered two witnesses; recall reached 91% and precision remained 92%.
Independently rebuild pinned environments, replay all 100 upgrades five times, and recompute precision and recall, including recovered witnesses.
Independent rebuilds changed tzdata despite fixed timezones, invalidating both recovered witnesses; recall fell from 91% to 88%.
Keep environment variants, pin tzdata digests, and withhold both recovered witnesses until independent replay restores ≥90% recall.
Pinning tzdata digests alongside JDK, locale, and timezone will restore independently reproducible witnesses and ≥90% recall and precision.
Rebuild tzdata-pinned containers independently, replay all UpgradeWitness cases five times, and recompute precision, recall, and witness stability.
With tzdata-pinned rebuilds, both recovered witnesses replayed 5/5 times; across 100 upgrades, recall reached 91% and precision 92%.
Have a second runner rebuild tzdata-pinned images from lockfiles, replay recovered witnesses, and audit all uncertain cases against labels.
Second runner resolved a different JDK vendor build; two recovered witnesses failed, reducing recall from 91% to 88%.
Retain tzdata pinning, additionally pin JDK vendor builds, and withhold both witnesses until cross-runner replay succeeds.
Use content-addressed runtime images pinning JDK vendor, tzdata, and OS to replay environment-sensitive witnesses across independent runners.
Will digest-pinned runtime images reproduce the two environment-sensitive witnesses across independent runners without sacrificing 92% precision?
Digest-pinned JDK-vendor, tzdata, and OS images will replay both witnesses across runners, yielding 91% recall and 92% precision.
Pin JDK-vendor, tzdata, and OS image digests; independently replay withheld witnesses five times and reassess 100-case precision and recall.
Rebuild digest-pinned JDK-vendor, tzdata, and OS images; replay both disputed witnesses across runners and recompute 100-case precision/recall.
Both disputed witnesses replayed 5/5 times on two digest-pinned runners; 100-case recall reached 91%, precision 92%.
On a third runner, verify image digests, replay every positive witness five times, and recompute labeled precision and recall.
Third-runner digest checks passed; all positive witnesses replayed 5/5 times, preserving 91% recall and 92% precision.
Adopt digest-pinned cross-runner replay for positive reports: witnesses reproduced 5/5, with 91% recall and 92% precision.
Implement verdict exporter using ReplayMatrix and digest-pinned cross-runner replay, attaching client reproduction commands and reflection/missing-code uncertainty tags.
ReplayMatrix v2 adds client-level verdicts, cross-runner image digests, replay commands, and explicit reflection/missing-code uncertainty labels.
Use client-constrained effect summaries to discard unreachable upstream changes, while marking paths through unavailable code or reflection uncertain.
Compute client-reachable effect summaries for changed methods, discard unreachable deltas, and require stable paired replays before attributing divergences.
Build effect summaries for changed methods across 100 upgrades, tracing client reachability and flagging reflection or missing-code paths.
EffectReach index maps changed methods to client entrypoints, observable effects, and explicit reflection or missing-code uncertainty edges.
Compare EffectReach-filtered ReplayMatrix v2 against unfiltered verdicts on 100 labeled upgrades, measuring precision, recall, witness replay, and uncertainty coverage.
EffectReach filtering cut recall from 91% to 86% by pruning client-reachable callbacks registered in unavailable code.
Restore unknown callback edges for unavailable registrars in EffectReach; rerun 100 upgrades to measure recovered recall and precision.
Unknown callback edges restored recall to 91%; EffectReach retained 92% precision and marked four opaque-registration cases uncertain.
Can unknown callback edges preserve recall without flooding analysts with uncertain reports for harmless upstream changes?
Requiring an observable-effect match for unknown callback edges will halve uncertain reports while maintaining ≥90% incompatibility recall.
On 100 labeled upgrades, require effect matches for unknown callback edges; compare opaque-registration uncertainty against four cases and 91% recall.
Effect matching reduced opaque-registration uncertainties from four to two; recall stayed 91% and precision 92% across 100 upgrades.
Adopt effect-matched unknown callback edges; unconditional pruning lost recall, while this retains 91% recall, 92% precision, and two uncertainties.
Instrument callback registration during client replay to resolve opaque targets, retaining unknown edges for unexercised paths.
Instrument effect-matched opaque registrations during pinned replays, resolve exercised callback targets, and retain uncertainty for unobserved registration paths.
Instrument opaque callback registrations in ReplayMatrix v2, map observed targets to EffectReach, and replay both uncertain cases five times.
ReplayMatrix v3 adds observed callback-target traces and retains unknown-target labels wherever registration paths remain unexercised.
Evaluate ReplayMatrix v3 on 100 upgrades, comparing callback uncertainty, recall, and precision against the four-case baseline and effect-matched filter.
ReplayMatrix v3 resolved one of two opaque-registration uncertainties; recall remained 91% and precision 92% across 100 upgrades.
Adopt callback tracing atop effect-matched unknown edges; it resolves one uncertainty without changing 91% recall or 92% precision.
Integrate ReplayMatrix v3 callback traces into the verdict exporter; run 100-case regression for recall, precision, witness replay, and uncertainty.
UpgradeAudit report bundles verdicts, client replay commands, pinned image digests, callback traces, and explicit unresolved reflection/missing-code uncertainty.
